brief: ROSE ENGINE: a guilloche lathe simulator that engraves intricate patterns like those on fine watch dials and banknotes. Model a rose engine: a rotating blank, a rosette cam (number of lobes, amplitude) rocking the headstock, a cutter that steps inward each pass, a phase shift per pass, plus a straight-line mode and a pumping mode. Patterns emerge cut by cut with animation, rendered as fine vector strokes on a metal disc with anisotropic metallic sheen, then an optional translucent enamel colour layer. Controls: lobes, amplitude, passes, phase per pass, cutter step, pattern presets with descriptive motif names (barleycorn, sunburst, basket weave, waves, flinque flame), engraving speed, metal (silver, gold, rose gold, blued steel). A short accurate note on rose-engine turning (ornamental lathes from the 1700s, later used on watch dials and Faberge enamel work). The first frame shows a finished gleaming dial with the next pattern starting to engrave.
